s: The Fourteenth Amendment says "No State shall…," and most constitutional rights restrain government, not private persons.
In the Civil Rights Cases (1883), the Court struck down the public-accommodations provisions of the Civil Rights Act of 1875 because § 5 reaches only state action.
The Thirteenth Amendment is the exception: it applies to private conduct.
Private conduct may nevertheless be attributed to the state.
Regulation, licensing, or public funding alone is not enough (Jackson v. Metropolitan Edison, 1974; Moose Lodge v. Irvis, 1972).
Congress may reach private conduct through other powers, notably the Commerce Clause (Civil Rights Act of 1964) and § 2 of the Thirteenth Amendment.
